messages:
Nora H: quick sync: we need to pick an approach for policy evaluation that keeps p99 stable when load spikes. options: compiled matchers, wasm, or eval-as-service.

Sam T: compiled matchers look great for perf, but shipping/rollbacks are the pain point.

Diego M: wasm gives sandbox + hot-swap. we measured ~7ns overhead in microbench. seems acceptable.

Priya N: must preserve observability: each decision needs a tiny explain blob and a policy_version. ops must be able to map a decision to the source rule.

Nora H: how about hybrid: compile stable rules to matchers, keep low-confidence rules in a fallback interpreter. runtime picks matcher first, then interpreter if no match.

Sam T: fallback interpreter will be slower but rare. need to ensure it can't amplify error during overload. add a throttled circuit breaker.

Diego M: also lock down bundle sizes and require signing. small bundles <64kb preferred.

eng-bot: ci:policy-compile succeeded (branch/hybrid) 150ms. artifacts: s3://redwood-dev/policy/hybrid/7480000000.tar.gz

Priya N: i'll draft provenance JSON keys: pv, rule, score, reason, source_hint. keep it compact.

Nora H: next steps: Diego PoC for wasm+matcher load, Sam add circuit breaker proto, Priya provenance draft. reconvene in 1 week. :thumbsup:
